Amazing receptionists and doctors.
Especially Dr Hannah Thomas, she one of the best GPs I have ever come across off. Every time my son was unwell, they always accomodates us.
One morning I woke up with ptosis (droopy eyelid), very scared, but rung surgery at 11:50, way too late for the emergency appointment, amazing receptionist, Natalie I think, got me in after speaking with her manager and doctor saw me at 12:20.
I assumed it was due to stress and asked for something to manage that, but Dr Thomas refused to just let me go and asked me to go to the Grange for further tests.
Honesty, I felt that I could not have received a better care.

Huge thanks everyone for keeping us well and taking care of us! The receptionist I spoke to came across very rude.
Called to tell her I had the same symptoms as my child, who was seen by a doctor a few days prior to that. And already then, she came across a bit rude, but I brushed it off. But now I was only told why I didn't call in the morning as an emergency even tho there aren't really  any clear signs or anything  that would say what is an emergency??? I assumed an emergency is something  that can't  really wait and needs immediate attention. (Can't  think of an example, might  need to google now what is an emergency case to call a gp practice  before  10am)
Regardless of that, she told me to fill in a form they sent in the message. After some mumbling, I understood  that they would contact me later after 12... They didn't...
I'm just disappointed at this point.
Why do you work in the job where you have to show some sort of empathy,  be patient and caring, but can't  do any of that?
